MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JULY 10, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR HUFF at 7:05 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling
Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Zerunyan and Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  Mitchell, Schmitz.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
  cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
  consideration will be voted on separately.)

  * MAYOR HUFF requested that ITEM 5E be removed for individual consideration. There
  being no objection, she so ordered. See below for action on 5E.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE REMAINING ITEMS AS PRESENTED
  BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JULY 10, 2018
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 26, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JUNE AND JUNE 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60184 THROUGH 60210 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $1,357,241.79; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 58213 (Void); 060118
  THROUGH 060618; 60059 THROUGH 60092; AND 60136 THROUGH 60174 IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $533,871.56 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,891,113.35
  WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JUNE 25, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  ANNUAL AUDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT – MACIAS GINI & O’CONNELL LLP (MGO)

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

* Item removed from Consent Calendar for individual consideration:

E.*  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE ATTENDANCE REPORT

  MAYOR HUFF expressed concern that based on the attendance report it seems as
  though there are some members of the Commissions and Committees that have not
  been attending meetings in 2018 and suggested that the COUNCIL discuss those
  attendance issues.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that the matter does warrant discussion
  and suggested that this matter be discussed when all COUNCIL MEMBERS are present.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE COMMISSION/COMMITTEE
  ATTENDANCE REPORT AND DIRECTED STAFF TO AGENDIZE THIS MATTER
  FOR DISCUSSION ON A FUTURE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA WHEN ALL
  COUNCILMEMBERS ARE PRESENT.

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 10, 2018
 6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  JUNE 5, 2018 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION – CERTIFICATION OF ELECTION
  RESULTS AND OATH OF OFFICE

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution 2429 declaring the results of
  the General Municipal Election held on June 5, 2018 and taking such further actions
  as provided by law to complete the election process.

  City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per agenda material) noting that Mayor Huff
  and Councilmember Zuckerman were both reelected to a four-term on the City Council
  and that Measure A was adopted by the voters.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION 2429 DECLARING THE
  RESULTS OF THE GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION HELD ON JUNE 5, 2018
  AND TAKING SUCH FURTHER ACTIONS AS PROVIDED BY LAW TO COMPLETE
  THE ELECTION PROCESS.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution 2429 by title.

  City Clerk Luce administered the Oath of Office and presented a Certificate of Election
  to Mayor Huff and Councilmember Zuckerman.

  MAYOR HUFF expressed her appreciation to the voters for reelecting her and shared the
  lessons she learned during this election process. She also shared her priorities for her
  second term in office including, developing neighborhood watch programs in each
  neighborhood to improve public safety and emergency preparedness; and developing a
  neighborhood council of representatives to create a cohesive citywide network to serve
  as source for leadership development. She also thanked COUNCILMEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN and congratulated him on his reelection.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN thanked the voters for their support and for
  supporting Measure A. He commented that the one of the biggest tasks before the City
  is updating the City’s General Plan and expressed the importance of this monumental
  task.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JULY 10, 2018
 B.  LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY FOR
  TEMPORARY CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT AND STORAGE YARD FACILITY LOCATED
  A THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached License Agreement for
  California Water Service Company and direct its execution all to the satisfaction of the
  City Attorney.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material) noting that the
  park planned for that location is still in the design development stage.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF, City Manager Prichard commented that based on the time
  needed to complete the various phases of the project design and approval, it is very
  unlikely that construction will begin before the beginning of 2019.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR
  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY AND DIRECTED ITS EXECUTION, TO
  THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

9.  OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis commented that since Measure A was adopted by the voters, it will be certified
by the City Clerk and become effective in 10 days with the new business license tax provisions
taking effect on January 1, 2019 as stated in the ordinance.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information
  and reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities
  of currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their
  various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest,
  which are not otherwise agendized.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that two cities, Rolling Hills Estates and South
Pasadena are now receiving power through the Clean Power Alliance and RHE has less than ½
of 1% of participants opting out.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JULY 10, 2018
 COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN also reported that the General Plan Advisory Committee
(GPAC) had a very productive meeting earlier this week with good participation. He encouraged
the public to attend the GPAC meetings and reminded everyone to visit the GPAC web site for
information on the process.

MAYOR HUFF commented that she attended the GPAC meeting as well and was very
impressed.

MAYOR HUFF reported that she was elected Chair of the SBCCOG Board of Directors at the
Board meeting on June 28, 2018. She also reported that City Manager Prichard was also
elected to serve as Chair the SBCCOG City Manager’s Association.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on
  currently pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized
  for future consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

MAYOR HUFF reminded those present and watching of several upcoming events including the
Tracy Austin Doubles Tournament scheduled for July 20-22, 2018 and National Night Out (NNO)
scheduled for August 7, 2018. She encouraged neighborhoods to participate in NNO.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 7:44 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Dick Moe
  for his many contributions to Rolling Hills Estates and the Peninsula community,
  including the Norris Theatre. The next regular meeting of the City Council is scheduled
  for Tuesday, July 24, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates
  City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JULY 10, 2018
